projects[].upstreamDefaultsUpstreamConfignilTemplate applied to every upstream (see inheritance rules in the upstreams section).
projects[].networks[]NetworkConfignilStatically declared chains; unlisted chains are lazily bootstrapped on first request.
projects[].networkDefaultsNetworkDefaultsnilShared defaults inherited by all networks (and lazy ones).
projects[].rateLimitBudgetstring""Names a budget in rateLimiters.budgets[]; unknown budget fails startup.
projects[].userAgentModestring"simplified""simplified" buckets User-Agent into ~20 low-cardinality names for the agent_name label; "raw" stores it verbatim (high cardinality). ?user-agent= query param wins over the header.
projects[].trustUserIdHeaderboolfalseRead the caller identity from the X-ERPC-User-Id header for the user metric/log label when no auth strategy resolved a user. eRPC does NOT validate the header — enable only behind a trusted proxy that sets and strips it.
projects[].forwardHeaders[]string (wildcards)nilIncoming headers matching these patterns are forwarded to upstream HTTP requests. Footgun: wildcard matches are stored under the pattern name, so X-Custom-* is forwarded as a literal X-Custom-* header. Exact names round-trip faithfully.
projects[].allowClientDirectivesstring (wildcard)nil (all allowed)Gates which X-ERPC-* request directives clients may use ("" = none; "!skip-cache-read & !use-upstream" = all except those). Config-set directiveDefaults always apply regardless. Does not filter X-ERPC-Force-Trace. Overridable per auth strategy.
projects[].ignoreMethods[]string (wildcards)nilMatching methods are rejected with JSON-RPC -32601 before auth/upstreams.
projects[].allowMethods[]string (wildcards)nilRe-allows methods ignored by ignoreMethods. Not an allowlist by itself — to build one use ignoreMethods: ["*"] + allowMethods: [...].
projects[].scoreMetricsWindowSizeDuration1m at runtime (source comments say 10m but the code value is 1 minute)Rolling window of the per-upstream health tracker (10 sliding buckets). Set 10m explicitly for a 10-minute window.
projects[].integrityIntegrityConfignilProject-wide data-integrity validation; a network-level integrity block overrides it.

projects[].cors.* (also admin.cors.*)

CORS is a soft deterrent: requests without an Origin header bypass CORS entirely, and disallowed origins still get a normal response (no Access-Control-* headers) — only the browser blocks them.

FieldTypeDefaultWhat it does
cors.allowedOrigins[]string (wildcards)["*"] — but required if a cors: block exists (validation error if empty)Matched against the Origin header. Remember . matches any char in glob patterns.
cors.allowedMethods[]string["GET","POST","OPTIONS"]Access-Control-Allow-Methods.
cors.allowedHeaders[]string["content-type","authorization","x-erpc-secret-token"]Access-Control-Allow-Headers.
cors.exposedHeaders[]stringnilAccess-Control-Expose-Headers. Nil sends an empty value, so browsers cannot read any X-ERPC-* response header — enumerate the ones your frontend needs.
cors.allowCredentialsboolfalseEmit Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true.
cors.maxAgeint (seconds)3600Access-Control-Max-Age (only when > 0).

Auth strategies (projects[].auth.strategies[])

auth.strategies is an ordered list; the first strategy whose type matches the extracted credential, that applies to the method, and that authenticates successfully wins. No strategies = allow-all. Credential extraction order (HTTP): ?token= (deprecated) → ?secret= → X-ERPC-Secret-Token header → Authorization: Basic (password half only) → Authorization: Bearer (JWT) → ?jwt= → ?signature=&message= (SIWE) → X-Siwe-Message/X-Siwe-Signature headers → network (client-IP) fallback.

FieldTypeDefaultWhat it does
strategies[].typestringinferred from sub-block"secret", "jwt", "siwe", "network", "database". Sub-block presence force-overwrites type for secret/database/jwt/siwe (order: secret→database→jwt→siwe) — never set two sub-blocks on one strategy. For network only type: "network" triggers auto-creation.
strategies[].ignoreMethods[]string (wildcards)nilStrategy skipped for matching methods.
strategies[].allowMethods[]string (wildcards)nilRe-applies the strategy when ignored.
strategies[].rateLimitBudgetstring""Strategy-level budget, applied after successful auth. A per-user budget (secret/siwe/network field, JWT claim, DB record) overrides it. Over-limit → 429.
strategies[].allowClientDirectivesstring (wildcard)nil (inherit project)Per-caller override of the project directive filter for users authenticated by this strategy.

secret strategy (strategies[].secret.*) — static token, for private server-to-server callers only (plain string comparison, not timing-safe):

FieldTypeDefaultWhat it does
secret.idstring""Becomes User.Id (metrics/log label).
secret.valuestringrequiredExact token to match. Redacted in config dumps.
secret.rateLimitBudgetstring""Per-secret budget attached to the returned user.

jwt strategy (strategies[].jwt.*) — verifies signed JWTs (RSA/EC/HMAC) with kid-based rotation and per-user budgets via a claim:

FieldTypeDefaultWhat it does
jwt.verificationKeysmap (kid → key)nilKey data is a PEM string, "file:///path", or bare HMAC secret. Empty map = deny-all (every JWT rejected).
jwt.verificationJwksUrlstring""Absolute HTTP(S) URL of a JWKS document; fetched at startup and refreshed in background. Static keys override same-kid JWKS entries. Must be absolute http(s) or startup fails.
jwt.verificationJwksRefreshIntervalDuration1hJWKS background refresh interval.
jwt.verificationJwksTlsInsecureSkipVerifyboolfalseSkip TLS verification for JWKS fetch (dev only).
jwt.allowedAlgorithms[]stringnil (any)e.g. ["RS256"]. Always restrict — nil allows algorithm-confusion attacks.
jwt.allowedIssuers[]stringnil (any)Exact iss match.
jwt.allowedAudiences[]stringnil (any)Exact scalar aud match — array-form aud claims always fail.
jwt.requiredClaims[]stringnilClaim names that must be present.
jwt.claimMatchersmap[string][]stringnilclaim → allowed values; AND across keys, OR within a list. Missing/empty claim → error.
jwt.rateLimitBudgetClaimNamestring"rlm"JWT claim read as the user's rate-limit budget.

siwe strategy (strategies[].siwe.*) — EIP-4361 Sign-In-With-Ethereum:

FieldTypeDefaultWhat it does
siwe.allowedDomains[]stringnil (deny-all)Exact match against the EIP-4361 domain field. Must list at least one domain.
siwe.rateLimitBudgetstring""Per-session budget. The recovered (lowercased) address becomes User.Id. Both ?signature= and ?message= (or the two headers) must be present together.

network strategy (strategies[].network.*) — IP allowlist, the credential-less fallback (any request without a token/JWT/SIWE payload lands here; put it first in the list if used):

FieldTypeDefaultWhat it does
network.allowedIPs[]stringnilExact IPs (invalid entry → startup error).
network.allowedCIDRs[]stringnilCIDR ranges (invalid entry → startup error).
network.allowLocalhostboolfalseAllow any loopback address unconditionally.
network.trustedProxies[]stringnilNo-op. Use server.trustedIPForwarders/trustedIPHeaders instead.
network.ipAsUserboolfalseCIDR matches: false → whole range shares one User.Id (the CIDR string); true → per-IP identity.
network.rateLimitBudgetstring""Budget for all matching IPs.

database strategy (strategies[].database.*) — dynamic API keys backed by a connector (postgresql, dynamodb, redis, memory, grpc), with in-process caching, singleflight dedup, retry, and a connector-down circuit breaker:

FieldTypeDefaultWhat it does
database.connectorConnectorConfigauto-created (id auth-<driver>)Where API keys live. Record JSON: {userId, enabled, rateLimitBudget?}.
database.maxWaitDuration1sPer-request timeout for the full DB lookup.
database.cache.ttlDuration1hPositive-cache TTL. Revoked keys keep working up to this long.
database.cache.maxSizeint10000Max cached keys.
database.cache.maxCostint1073741824 (1 GiB)Ristretto cost budget.
database.cache.numCountersint100000Ristretto counters (also used by the negative cache).
database.retry.maxAttemptsint3DB lookup attempts.
database.retry.baseBackoffDuration100msBackoff per attempt: base << (attempt-1).
database.failOpen.enabledboolfalseOn DB errors, grant an emergency user instead of rejecting.
database.failOpen.userIdstring"emergency-failopen"Identity for fail-open traffic.
database.failOpen.rateLimitBudgetstring""Budget for fail-open traffic (set one — cap the blast radius).

Negative cache: hardcoded 5 s TTL (not configurable). The connector-down breaker fast-paths to fail-open and probes the DB at ~1 query/second per replica.

Integrity (projects[].integrity / networks[].integrity)

Opt-in data-integrity validation. level is the front-door preset: off | intrinsic | corroborated | authoritative.

FieldTypeDefaultWhat it does
integrity.levelstring"" (off)Preset selecting the check tier. A network block merges over the project block (network wins).
integrity.checksmapnilPer-check overrides keyed by catalog id: {enabled, params, onFailure: recordOnly|hardReject}.
integrity.budgetobjectnilCaps authoritative-tier canonical fetches: {maxPerSecond, maxConcurrent}.
integrity.autoCorrectWhenPossiblebooltrueOn violation, hunt a validated replacement (retry/hedge) before applying the verdict.
integrity.invalidBehaviorobjectnilPer-finality verdict (recordOnly/hardReject/off, split finalized vs not) for reorg-sensitive checks. Deterministic checks always hardReject.
integrity.reorgWindowint32Blocks back from the tip the ChainView pins number→hash. Raise for deep-reorg chains.
integrity.observeOnlyboolfalseRun every check but never let a verdict touch the response; violations recorded as would_reject. The safe way to roll out integrity. Absolute — overrides everything.
integrity.stateProbeobjectoffPer-upstream state-trie proofs: {enabled, interval (default 2s)}. Records misbehavior; never routes.
integrity.followobjectoffChain follower: {enabled, interval (default 1s), maxBlocksPerTick (default 16)}. Costs one eth_getBlockByNumber per block per network.
integrity.misbehaviorsDestinationobjectnilJSONL forensic export (same shape as consensus misbehaviorsDestination: type file/s3, path, filePattern, s3 flush knobs).
integrity.headerModestring"off"Whether per-request X-ERPC-Integrity headers may adjust integrity: off / profiles / full.
integrity.profilesmapnilNamed IntegritySettings blocks selectable by header when headerMode permits.

projects[].networks[]

One entry per chain. Networks not listed are lazily bootstrapped on first request from the project's providers/upstreams. The network metric label is the alias when set, otherwise the raw id (evm:1, svm:mainnet-beta).

networks[].multiplexingboolenabled (nil)In-flight identical-request dedup (leader/follower).

FieldTypeDefaultWhat it does

evm.integrity.enforceNonNullTaggedBlocksbooltrueDeprecated — same migration.

evm.servedTip.*

Default ("max mode") returns the MAX latest/finalized across eligible, non-syncing upstreams — which can jump backwards across pods. Listing a tag switches that axis to a cluster-corroborated, monotonic pick via shared state.

FieldTypeDefaultWhat it does
servedTip.enabledFor[]string[] (max mode)latest, finalized, safe (safe resolves to the finalized axis). Listing a tag enables the corroborated cluster tip for it.
servedTip.clusterDeltaint64—Deprecated/ignored (former cluster picker; majority order statistic needs no tuning). Kept for parse compatibility.
servedTip.guaranteedMethods[]string (glob)[]Methods whose supporting-upstream subset must be able to serve the advertised latest (membership auto-detected; no per-upstream config).
servedTip.maxRegressionBlocksint640 → 1024How far below the corroborated live head the majority pick may fall before it is treated as poisoned and the last corroborated pick is served instead. -1 disables the guard.
servedTip.trajectoryWindowDuration10mHead-history window for the trajectory referee (stall detection). Explicit 0 disables the referee. Write as a duration string — bare numbers are milliseconds.

FieldTypeDefaultWhat it does

svm.commitmentstringnonefinalized, confirmed, or processed. Pins one commitment level across the pool so cache and consensus compare like-for-like; unset leaves each node's default in charge.

Known Solana clusters validate the genesis hash at bootstrap (mismatch or fetch failure fails the upstream). Unknown (chain, cluster) pairs validate only when the upstream sets svm.checkGenesisHash: true (see upstreams).

FieldTypeDefaultWhat it does
methods.preserveDefaultMethodsboolfalseCritical: false + any definitions entry replaces ALL built-in method definitions (hundreds, incl. eth_call/eth_getLogs) with only your entries. true copies built-ins first, then merges yours. false + no definitions keeps everything (same as omitting).

definitions.<m>.finalizedboolfalse (true for static-cache methods)Marks responses immutable. Never set on non-finalized data — every response is then cached permanently at the first value returned.
definitions.<m>.realtimeboolfalse (true for eth_blockNumber-like)Forces realtime finality → short-TTL cache bucket.

definitions.<m>.translateLatestTagboolenabled"latest" replaced with the current block hex before forwarding/cache-keying. false on a changing method collapses all callers to one "latest" cache key. eth_getBlockByNumber ships false to discover new blocks.

definitions.<m>.enforceBlockAvailabilityboolnil (inherit)Per-method override of block-availability gating; highest priority.
definitions.<m>.reqRefs / respRefs[][]pathbuilt-insWhere to find the block ref in the request/response (drives cache keying). Custom values replace built-ins entirely — no merge.

Block-availability bounds — each bound sets exactly one of:

Sub-fieldTypeDefaultMeaning
{lower,upper}.latestBlockMinusint64nilBound = latest block − N (recomputed each check from the poller).
{lower,upper}.earliestBlockPlusint64nilBound = detected earliest block + N (probe-detected).

When every upstream skips a block, the client gets JSON-RPC code -32014 ("block not available"). A computed min > max fails open (WARN + upstream serves any block).

svm.chainstring"" → "solana"; inheritedChain this upstream serves; must match the network's chain. "" cannot serve a fork network.
svm.checkGenesisHashboolfalseOpts an unknown (chain, cluster) pair into getGenesisHash validation at bootstrap. Known Solana clusters always validate (fail-closed).

upstreams[].jsonRpc.*

FieldTypeDefaultWhat it does
jsonRpc.supportsBatchboolfalseEnable outbound JSON-RPC batching.
jsonRpc.batchMaxSizeint0Max requests per batch. 0 with batching on fires on the first queued request — use ≥ 2 to coalesce.
jsonRpc.batchMaxWaitDuration0Wait before flushing a partial batch. 0 fires immediately — set ≥ 10ms for real coalescing.
jsonRpc.enableGzipboolfalseCompress outbound request bodies. Responses are always decompressed.
jsonRpc.headersmapnilStatic headers on every outbound request (Header.Set, overwrites defaults). Footgun: ≥2 entries make the client cache key order-unstable (map iteration), re-creating the client per call.
jsonRpc.proxyPoolstring""Outbound proxy pool id (must exist in proxyPools[]).

Outbound HTTP transport constants (not configurable): MaxIdleConns 1024, MaxIdleConnsPerHost 256, MaxConnsPerHost unlimited, IdleConnTimeout 90s, ResponseHeaderTimeout 30s, TLSHandshakeTimeout 10s, end-to-end client timeout 60s, dial timeout 10s, TCP keepalive 15s.

upstreams[].routing.*

FieldTypeDefaultWhat it does
routing.scoreMultipliers[][]objectunset = 1Per-network/method score scaling: entries {network, method, overall, errorRate, respLatency, throttledRate, blockHeadLag, finalizationLag, misbehaviors}. overall: 2 = twice as preferred; 0 on a dimension removes its contribution.
routing.scoreLatencyQuantilefloat0 → policy default p70Which latency quantile feeds scoring.
routing.probestring"" → "on""off" opts this upstream out of probe-excluded shadow-mirror traffic.

upstreams[].shadow.*

FieldTypeDefaultWhat it does
shadow.enabledboolfalseRegisters the upstream as a shadow: never serves real traffic; receives async mirrored clones of real responses.
shadow.sampleRatefloatnil → 1.0Probability a real response triggers a mirror.
shadow.ignoreFieldsmap[string][]stringnilPer-method response fields ignored during shadow comparison.

upstreamDefaults inheritance semantics

  • Scalars (endpoint, type, vendorName, rateLimitBudget, autoIgnoreUnsupportedMethods): inherited individually when unset.
  • tags, failsafe, routing: all-or-nothing — any local value replaces the defaults entirely.
  • evm sub-fields: per-field merge when both sides non-nil.
  • svm sub-fields: no local block → wholesale copy; partial block → empty fields filled.
  • jsonRpc: shallow copy only when the upstream has no jsonRpc block.

projects[].providers[]

One API key expands into an upstream per chain the vendor supports.

FieldTypeDefaultWhat it does
providers[].idstringrequiredUnique per project; upstream ids derive from it via upstreamIdTemplate.
providers[].vendorstringrequiredVendor key (e.g. alchemy, drpc, repository, envio; 20+ supported).
providers[].settingsmapnilVendor-specific (redacted in dumps) — e.g. apiKey. Common key: creditUnits (per-method CU overrides).
providers[].onlyNetworks[]stringnilRestrict expansion to these networks. Bypasses vendor support checks entirely (a listed network is always "supported"). Evaluated after ignoreNetworks.
providers[].ignoreNetworks[]stringnilExclude these networks from expansion.
providers[].upstreamIdTemplatestringvendor default (e.g. {{.Provider}}-{{.ChainId}})Template for generated upstream ids.
providers[].overridesmap (chain → UpstreamConfig)nilPer-chain upstream overrides (e.g. a specific rateLimitBudget or failsafe for one chain).

Failsafe policies (failsafe[] entries)

A failsafe[] list appears at three scopes: networks[].failsafe[], upstreams[].failsafe[], and cache-connector failsafeForGets/failsafeForSets. Each entry is selected by first-match on the envelope fields; one entry may carry several policies (retry + hedge + timeout + consensus compose: consensus(retry(hedge(...)))).

Envelope selector fields

FieldTypeDefaultWhat it does
failsafe[].matchMethodstring (wildcard)"*"Method pattern. Empty string is a validation error after defaults.
failsafe[].matchFinality[]string[] (any)Subset of finalized, unfinalized, realtime, unknown. Executor selection priority: method+finality > method > finality > catch-all.

Scope rules: circuitBreaker at network scope and consensus at upstream scope are startup errors (ErrFailsafeConfiguration).

retry (RetryPolicyConfig)

Network-scope retry = a fresh full upstream sweep per attempt (the failover mechanism). Upstream-scope retry = re-hitting the same upstream for transport blips. They compose multiplicatively (3 × 3 = up to 9 physical calls).

FieldTypeDefaultWhat it does
retry.maxAttemptsintnetwork 5 (injected default) / system 3 / upstream 1Total execution rounds including the first. 1 = no retries.
retry.delayDuration0Base delay before the first retry (0 = immediate; does NOT disable retry).
retry.backoffFactorfloat1.2Exponential multiplier per 0-indexed attempt. Must be > 0.
retry.backoffMaxDelayDuration3sBackoff cap before jitter. Must be non-zero.
retry.jitterDuration0Uniform random additive jitter [0, jitter).
retry.emptyResultAccept[]string["eth_getLogs","trace_filter","arbtrace_filter","eth_call","eth_getBalance","eth_getCode","eth_getStorageAt","eth_getTransactionCount"]Methods where empty/null is valid data — no retry.
retry.emptyResultIgnore[]stringnilDeprecated alias for emptyResultAccept; used only when the latter is nil (no merge).
retry.emptyResultMaxAttemptsint2Shared cap (INCLUDING the first attempt) for all data-unavailability reasons (empty_result, missing_data, block_unavailable, pending_tx) across ALL retry rounds. 1 = zero empty-retries.
retry.emptyResultDelayDuration0Static fallback delay before data-unavailability retries only while the EMA block time is cold; the warm dynamic delay (EMA × blockUnavailableDelayMultiplier) overrides it unconditionally. Not a floor. Set ~1s for Ethereum cold-start safety.
retry.blockUnavailableDelayDuration0Deprecated — merged into emptyResultDelay when that is 0, then cleared.

Related fields outside retry: directiveDefaults.retryEmpty / retryPending, evm.blockUnavailableDelayMultiplier (default 1.0), evm.emptyResultConfidence (blockHead), evm.markEmptyAsErrorMethods.

hedge (HedgePolicyConfig)

Races a backup request on another upstream when the primary is silent; first kept result wins, siblings are cancelled. Write methods are excluded (eth_sendRawTransaction is the deliberate exception — idempotent broadcast).

FieldTypeDefaultWhat it does
hedge.delayDuration or {base, quantile, min, max}— (no hedge if absent)Scalar = static delay. Object = adaptive: clamp(quantile_of_method_latency + base, min, max).
hedge.delay.baseDuration0Static addend; with quantile: 0 this IS the delay (min/max ignored).
hedge.delay.quantilefloat0 (static)Per-method latency percentile [0,1] from the network's QuantileTracker. Requires base or max.
hedge.delay.minDuration100ms (auto-set when 0)Floor in quantile mode; also the cold-start fallback (never set 0 manually — cold-start hedges fire immediately).
hedge.delay.maxDuration999s (auto-set when 0)Ceiling in quantile mode.
hedge.maxCountint1 (2 in the no-projects system template)Max ADDITIONAL attempts beyond the primary. 0 disables hedging silently.

Legacy siblings hedge.quantile / minDelay / maxDelay are folded into delay.* only for sub-fields the object form left at zero.

timeout (TimeoutPolicyConfig)

Three nested layers: server.maxTimeout (hard ceiling) > network-scope timeout (bounds the whole retry+hedge lifecycle) > upstream-scope timeout (bounds one upstream's attempts). Lifecycle-scoped, not per-attempt: a 500 ms network timeout with maxAttempts: 3 is 500 ms total, not per attempt. Zero/nil disables the timeout for that scope (fail-open).

FieldTypeDefaultWhat it does
timeout.durationDuration or {base, quantile, min, max}network 120s / upstream 60sThe budget. Scalar = static. Object = adaptive per-method quantile.
timeout.duration.baseDuration0Static value / quantile addend / cold-start first fallback.
timeout.duration.quantilefloat0 (static)Per-method latency percentile. Always set base or max — quantile-only is fail-open on cold start.
timeout.duration.minDurationauto-floor base/2 (or 500ms when base=0) at build timeFloor preventing feedback-loop collapse. Explicit 0 bypasses the floor.
timeout.duration.maxDuration0 (uncapped)Ceiling; cold-start fallback of last resort.

Legacy flat siblings timeout.quantile / minDuration / maxDuration fold into duration.* with the same precedence (object wins).

circuitBreaker (CircuitBreakerPolicyConfig)

Per-upstream in-process breaker; trips when the failure ring buffer fills with enough failures, blocks traffic without dialing, probes after a cooldown. Also valid on cache connectors (where the connector's own timeout expiry counts as a failure). Startup error at network scope.

FieldTypeDefaultWhat it does
circuitBreaker.failureThresholdCountuint20Failures required to trip. Must be ≤ capacity. Evaluated only once the window is FULL.
circuitBreaker.failureThresholdCapacityuint80Ring-buffer size (last-N outcomes).
circuitBreaker.halfOpenAfterDuration5mCooldown before a probe is admitted. Must exceed the upstream's real restart time or the breaker flaps.
circuitBreaker.successThresholdCountuint8Successes required in the HalfOpen trial to re-close. Must be ≤ capacity.
circuitBreaker.successThresholdCapacityuint200 (not 10 — the 10 defaults block is unreachable dead code)HalfOpen trial window size; also caps concurrent HalfOpen permits. Set explicitly for fast re-close decisions.

Hedge attempts and internal poller probes bypass the breaker entirely (no permit check, no outcome recording).

consensus (ConsensusPolicyConfig)

Fans a request out to N upstreams, groups identical responses by hash, and declares a winner when enough agree; misbehaving upstreams can be cordoned automatically. Network scope only (startup error at upstream scope). Skip per request via X-ERPC-Skip-Consensus: true / ?skip-consensus=true.

FieldTypeDefaultWhat it does
consensus.maxParticipantsint5Upstreams to fan out to (clamped ≥ 1).
consensus.agreementThresholdint2Minimum participants agreeing on one response hash. Also the low-participants bar.
consensus.disputeBehaviorstring"returnError"When enough participants respond but no group meets the threshold: returnError, acceptMostCommonValidResult, preferBlockHeadLeader, onlyBlockHeadLeader.
consensus.lowParticipantsBehaviorstring"acceptMostCommonValidResult"When too few valid participants (upstreams unreachable/errors): same four values.
consensus.disputeLogLevelstring"warn"Zerolog level for misbehavior events (trace…error).
consensus.ignoreFieldsmap[method][]stringeth_getLogs: ["*.blockTimestamp"], eth_getTransactionReceipt: ["blockTimestamp","logs.*.blockTimestamp"], eth_getBlockReceipts: ["*.blockTimestamp","*.logs.*.blockTimestamp"]Dot-paths excluded from the canonical hash. Full replacement — setting any entry drops all three defaults; re-include them when extending.
consensus.preferNonEmptybooltruePrefer non-empty over empty/error in dispute resolution.
consensus.preferLargerResponsesbooltruePrefer larger bodies; disables ALL short-circuit (every request waits for all participants). Disable for latency.
consensus.preferHighestValueFormap[method][]fieldsnilRegroup by extracted numeric value (hex/decimal aware); highest ≥ threshold wins. For fee/nonce reads (eth_gasPrice, eth_getTransactionCount → ["result"]). Bypasses all other rules.
consensus.fireAndForgetboolfalseAfter short-circuit, remaining goroutines keep running detached (context.WithoutCancel) — for eth_sendRawTransaction broadcast. Survives client disconnect AND shutdown signals.
consensus.maxWaitOnResultAdaptiveDuration{quantile: 0.5, min: 5ms, max: 1s}Cap after the first non-empty response. Cold start falls back to min.
consensus.maxWaitOnEmptyAdaptiveDuration{quantile: 0.9, min: 50ms, max: 2s}Cap after the first response of any kind.
consensus.requiredParticipants[][]object[] (disabled){tag (glob, required), minParticipants (required >0), minAgreement (0=off)}. Front-loads tag-matching upstreams; minAgreement is hard-enforced (violations → composition dispute).
consensus.punishMisbehaviorobjectnil{disputeThreshold (required >0), disputeWindow (required >0), sitOutPenalty}. Token-bucket cordon punishment for persistent misbehavior (needs a strict majority consensus group).
consensus.misbehaviorsDestinationobjectnilJSONL forensic export of misbehavior rounds. {type: file|s3, path, filePattern, s3:{maxRecords: 100, maxSize: 1MiB, flushInterval: 60s, region, contentType, credentials}}. S3 uses PutObject (overwrites); YAML key accessKeyID casing is load-bearing.

Special case: eth_sendRawTransaction returns the first non-empty response immediately regardless of threshold (broadcast mode).

15. Directives & execution headers

Per-request directives override behavior without touching config — set them as HTTP headers or query params (query wins). Client-set directives can be restricted per project with allowClientDirectives.

Directive headerQuery paramWhat it does
X-ERPC-Retry-Emptyretry-emptyRetry when an upstream answers empty/null
X-ERPC-Retry-Pendingretry-pendingPoll tx-lookup methods until the tx is mined
X-ERPC-Skip-Cache-Readskip-cache-readBypass the cache (all connectors, or a matching id)
X-ERPC-Use-Upstreamuse-upstreamPin the request to an upstream by id, glob, or tag
X-ERPC-Skip-Interpolationskip-interpolationKeep block tags (latest) instead of hex in outbound params
X-ERPC-Skip-Consensusskip-consensusBypass consensus; retry + hedge still apply

Every response carries execution headers (server.executionHeaders: all | summary | off):

HeaderTells you
X-ERPC-CacheHIT or MISS
X-ERPC-UpstreamWhich upstream served the response
X-ERPC-UpstreamsPer-attempt trace: id, role, outcome, duration
X-ERPC-Attempts / X-ERPC-Network-Retries / X-ERPC-Upstream-HedgesHow hard eRPC worked for this answer
X-ERPC-Consensus-Slots / X-ERPC-Consensus-DisputesConsensus participation and disagreements

Auth strategies: secret (API key), database (connector-backed keys), jwt (JWKS), siwe (Sign-In with Ethereum), network (IP/CIDR allowlist).

Built-in vendors (one key unlocks every chain they support): alchemy, ankr, blastapi, blockdaemon, blockpi, chainstack, conduit, drpc, dwellir, envio, erpc, etherspot, goldsky, infura, llama, onfinality, pimlico, quicknode, repository, routemesh, satelink, superchain, tenderly, thirdweb.

16. Glossary

  • Project — the tenant container in your config (projects[].id); owns auth, upstreams, and networks. First URL segment.
  • Network — one chain inside a project, e.g. evm:42161. Owns the cache, failsafe policies, and selection policy.
  • Upstream — a single RPC endpoint eRPC can call (yours or a vendor's).
  • Failsafe — eRPC's resilience policies: retry, hedge, timeout, circuitBreaker, consensus.
  • Hedge — a speculative parallel copy of your request, fired after an adaptive delay; first good answer wins.
  • Consensus — asking several upstreams and returning the answer at least agreementThreshold of them agree on.
  • Finality — how settled the data is: finalized, unfinalized, realtime, unknown. Drives cache TTLs.
  • Selection policy — a JS evalFunc that re-orders upstreams using live health metrics, evaluated on an interval.
  • Multiplexing — identical in-flight requests share one upstream call.
  • Cordon — operational exclusion of an upstream (per method or entirely) without undeploying it.
  • Shadow upstream — receives a sampled mirror of traffic for comparison; its answers are never served.
  • Directive — a per-request override via X-ERPC-* header, query param, or directiveDefaults.

17. Where to start reading the source

A curated reading order, following one request end to end and then branching into the subsystems:

  1. erpc/http_server.go — createRequestHandler, parseUrlPath, batch fan-out, response headers. The front door.
  2. erpc/networks.go — Network.Forward: static responses → multiplexer → cache read → selection ordering → sweep. The heart of the system.
  3. erpc/network_executor.go — networkExecutor.Run, shouldRetryWithReason, runHedge. The failsafe composition.
  4. erpc/multiplexer.go + Network.handleMultiplexing in erpc/networks.go — leader/follower dedup and byte-perfect fan-out.
  5. upstream/upstream.go — Upstream.Forward: availability gate, budget permit, breaker, health recording.
  6. consensus/executor.go + consensus/rules.go — participant slots, canonical hashing, unassailable lead, disputes.
  7. architecture/evm/json_rpc_cache.go — finality-aware cache keys, age guard, write guard.
  8. internal/policy/ — the selection-policy engine: slot ticks, sobek eval, sticky primary, probing.

Then the chain-specific packages — architecture/svm/ for Solana, architecture/evm/eth_getLogs.go for range splitting, common/errors.go for the error taxonomy — and the operator surfaces: auth/, data/ connectors, and telemetry/metrics.go.

Sources: the erpc/erpc repository and the deep dives at docs.erpc.cloud/inside-erpc. Compiled 2026-09-16. Line numbers refer to the repository state at compile time and will drift; symbol names are the stable index.
